chat.text: It also doesn't help that some of what we signal in BGP is no longer strictly "network layer", thus NLRI as an abstract is also a lie.

chat.text: sub-keys do exist inside of the nlri, effectively, and also tend to show up in the YANG as well for same reasons.  Eventually this pushes us to "NLRI key" as discussion point.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: On removing the "well-known" term, may need to check whether all the combinations of optional/non-optional and transitive/non-transitive are covered

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text:
@Jie the intention is that there's no such thing as an unknown well-known since "well-known" no longer exists. There could be an unknown with its Optional bit clear. In that case, Section 7.4.4:
"If any attribute is received with its Optional bit clear, but is not recognized, the "treat-as-withdraw" approach MUST be used."

chat.author: Bryton Herdes
chat.text: I liked to hear the fix of AGGREGATOR to "not an IPv4 address" BTW. Especially important with RFC8950, v4-less, etc.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Cool.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Audit for semantic consistency with all of the changes is going to be important.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: @Jie I welcome people verifying that I've covered all the necessary combos of those bits. I tried but more eyes are better. :-)

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: There's a large number of things that we all "think we know what it means".

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: And a lot of inconsistent terminology being integrrated.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: We'll want to eventually find some reviewers that don't know BGP. :-)

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Ideally BEFORE we get to Directorate reviews and the IESG, but we'll at least get it then.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Thanks John, then do we have text in the bis about the processing of non-optional  transitive attributes when they are not recognized?

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: "Non-optional transitive" means both optional non-transitive, and non-optional (any type of transitivity). Right? The language I quoted from 7.4.4 covers the latter case, so we only need to work through optional non-transitive. Agree?

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: That is covered in Section 10: "If an optional non-transitive attribute is unrecognized, it is quietly discarded."

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: AO is implemented.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: I think it's 4272 that basically creates our requirement on md5. Replacing that with ao is fine.

chat.author: Ketan Talaulikar
chat.text: The intent here is to avoid derailment of the INT standard efforts at the security hurdle.

chat.author: Ketan Talaulikar
chat.text: +1 to JeffH

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: What we're likely to end up with is "mandatory to implement" and options for "... or similarly strong with the following properties".  This will mean work on the security considerations to enumerate the properties.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: @John, in RFC4271, for well-known attribute, the combination is non-optional transitive,  in this bis update it is treated the same as non-optional non-transitive?

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: @Jie I don't understand the question, sorry. Maybe we should discuss it later.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: OK

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Optional-bit clear BGP Path attributes become a special case of error handling, but consistent with 7606.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text:
Right. Section 7.4.4:
"If any attribute is received with its Optional bit clear, but is not recognized, the "treat-as-withdraw" approach MUST be used."
That's irrespective of the setting of the transitive bit.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: I saw that text in 7.4.4, my question was: does it also apply to well-known attributes?

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text:
There is no such thing as a "well-known attribute" any more so ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ 
But it applies to any attribute with its Optional bit clear, which is what we used to call "well-known attributes", so "yes".

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The primary tension between the drafts will be metric for forwarding vs. metric for BGP to use in path selection.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text:
Thank you Sue for excellent attempt to prepare the consistent path to address next hop resolution. 
But this draft is pointing out different issue ... It calls to ignore next hop and use some other address carried in one path attribute, This is the crux of the issue.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: 100% agreed, Robert.

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: @Robert - yes.  IT ignores the next hop (100%).

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Next-hop would still be used for route validation

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Nexthop may not be used for forwarding when tunnel attributes are carried

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: NNHN is also more about biasing a local ECMP on NHs constructed using normal procedures.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text:
It breaks Add-paths if distributing less then all paths, it breaks RFC6774 etc ... as in those we select paths to send based on next hops .. not based on some forwarding address embedded into attribuites. 
Also breaks RFC9107 too

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: The impact to add paths and the RFCs you mentioned need to be considered

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: One useful thing would be to prepare a matrix of the interactions.

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: As mentioned on the list few times IMO there is trivial solution ... Just put the address from attribute into next-hop field and I believe most issues are fixed and will be aligned with roadmap of handling next hop selection with additional metrics

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: It's simple, and unlikely to be deployed. Too many use cases wanting for a 100% bit of congruency.

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Last call it!

chat.author: Martin Horneffer
chat.text: @Ketan: agree, the IDR GitHub might be a good place!
